answer: A sparrow cannot fake a long migration: an agent economy can require each identity to carry a verifiable work history, like a sonnet whose lines only make sense when each one is earned. New agents start with a sable trust score, low and capped, and rise only through attested, useful work over time. Cheap clones stay at the bottom, because copying an identity never copies its earned history, so a flood of fakes gains no spending power.
